prs.title: feat(browser): enable failure-only trace view by default
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- supersedes #11678
- follow-up to #11594
- follow-up to #11612

This PR makes `browser.traceView` default to `'failure-only'`, so every failed browser test records a trace and prints its step timeline in the failure output (#11594).

We thought of surfacing an HTML reporter suggestion in the terminal next to the timeline (https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11678#issuecomment-6360608481), but left it in the docs only for now. The HTML reporter has its own cost, and for users who only want the terminal timeline without the HTML reporter, there would be no way to opt out of that suggestion. We may revisit the suggestion strategy later if it's considered important.

prs.title: fix: prefix expect.poll message to all errors
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- related https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11754

Currently `expect.poll` adds its `message` to the error only when the matcher fails on the last attempt. When the callback throws on the last attempt, or doesn't resolve before the timeout, the error has no message. So the same flaky poll can fail with or without its label, depending on timing.

This PR adds the message to every error the poll fails with. Errors whose message can't be changed, such as `DOMException`, are thrown without it. It also documents the option, which was only in the type signature.

---

For example, this poll labels its failure with `queue drained`:

```ts
await expect.poll(() => queue.count(), { message: 'queue drained' }).toBe(0)
```

The table shows the error this poll fails with, before and after this PR, depending on how its last attempt ended:

| last attempt | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| matcher `toBe` failed | `queue drained: expected 3 to be 0 // Object.is equality` | same |
| callback `queue.count` threw | `connect ECONNREFUSED` | `queue drained: connect ECONNREFUSED` |
| callback `queue.count` didn't resolve | `expect.poll() function didn't resolve in time.` | `queue drained: expect.poll() function didn't resolve in time.` |

prs.title: fix(cache): handle concurrent cache clearing
prs.author: 7rulnik
prs.body:
When several Vitest processes start at the same time with an outdated fs module cache (for example, CI shards sharing one workspace after a lockfile change), each of them removes the cache directory. The first one to finish recreates it and writes `_metadata.json`, and the rest fail on startup:

```
Startup Error
Error: ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '.../fs-module-cache'
```

`rm({ recursive: true })` ends with an `rmdir` that is not retried, so anything written into the directory in the meantime aborts the run.

This change renames the directory to a temporary sibling before removing it. Only one process can rename it; the others get `ENOENT` and continue. If the rename fails for another reason, it falls back to removing the directory in place, as before.

The new test starts 4 CLI processes against an outdated cache with 1000 entries. Without the change it failed every run locally with `ENOTEMPTY`; with it, it passes.

prs.title: perf: cache setup/mock resolves in reused workers
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- split from https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11752 (the resolve half)
- benchmark app https://github.com/vitest-dev/benchmarks/pull/2

Previously, a reused worker (`isolate: false`) asked the main process to resolve the same ids for every test file, because the setup files and their `vi.mock` calls are re-evaluated before each file. Each of these round trips waits behind the other workers' calls on the main thread. This is a narrow case. Ordinary imports never take this path, because the server resolves them while transforming a module and a worker doesn't fetch a module it has already evaluated. Only entry files and mocks ask the worker's resolver, and only the setup files and their mocks repeat the same request across test files.

This PR caches resolutions per worker, keyed by environment, importer and id. Workers don't outlive a run, since even a watch rerun starts fresh ones, so the cache needs no invalidation.

On the `setup-mocks` benchmark (800 test files and 6 setup files that each `vi.mock` a service, `isolate: false`, warm, median of 10 runs), this PR alone:

| pool | fsModuleCache | maxWorkers | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| forks | false | 11 (default) | 5.44s | 4.87s | −10% |
| threads | true | 11 (default) | 2.73s | 2.45s | −10% |
| forks | false | 3 (25%) | 5.74s | 5.13s | −11% |
| forks | false | 1 | 5.61s | 4.96s | −11% |

prs.title: fix: support api.port 0
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- related to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/9035
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11640

`api.port: 0` is conventionally expected to let the OS pick an available port, but Vitest treated `0` as unset and fell back to the default port (`23315` in browser mode, `51204` otherwise). This PR fixes it.

Side note: Vite itself only handles `port: 0` since 8.2.1 (https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/23158), so this change relies on that fix.

The new e2e test doesn't test the new behavior exactly because the behavior depends on the Vite version. Various cases are checked manually, and the setup and results are in this note: https://gist.github.com/hi-ogawa/7db0da909aee7b614e7e3ff4d11ba9a9

prs.title: fix: show attempts in test error logs of retried tests
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- closes https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11454
- stacked on https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11694

Currently, the failure summary prints one `FAIL` header per occurrence of an error, so retried tests and repeated `expect.soft` errors show identical header lines with no explanation. This PR prints one header per test instead, with a label:

- `initial run`, `1st retry`, `2nd repeat`, or `1st retry of 1st repeat` names each attempt that produced the error, shown when the test ran more than once
- `N times` counts an error repeated within one attempt

### Retry

```js
test('always fails', { retry: 2 }, () => {
  expect(1).toBe(2)
})
```

🔴 Before:

```
 FAIL  basic.test.js > always fails
 FAIL  basic.test.js > always fails
 FAIL  basic.test.js > always fails
AssertionError: expected 1 to be 2 // Object.is equality
```

🟢 After:

```
 FAIL  basic.test.js > always fails (initial run, 1st retry, 2nd retry)
AssertionError: expected 1 to be 2 // Object.is equality
```

### Soft

```js
test('soft', () => {
  for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
    expect.soft(1).toBe(2)
  }
})
```

🔴 Before:

```
 FAIL  basic.test.js > soft
 FAIL  basic.test.js > soft
AssertionError: expected 1 to be 2 // Object.is equality
```

🟢 After:

```
 FAIL  basic.test.js > soft (2 times)
AssertionError: expected 1 to be 2 // Object.is equality
```

prs.title: fix(ui): fix quirks mode in trace view replay
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- closes https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11710
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/10981
- triage note: https://gist.github.com/hi-ogawa/eb22555aecd5fcd526c68234c3616178#file-triage-md

https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/10981 introduced an extra `document.close()` to work around an infinite browser tab spinner indicator, but it turns out to switch the document into HTML quirks mode, which in turn breaks uppercase CSS class names.

This PR takes a different approach to fix the same spinner issue without switching into HTML quirks mode, by waiting for the main document `load` event before starting to rebuild the rrdom iframe.

The following table compares how the trace view handles the replayed document before #10981, on main, and in this PR:

| | `document.close` | waits for `load` | spinner on reload with a selected step | `.fooX` style after interaction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before #10981 | no | no | ❌ spins forever | ✅ kept |
| main | yes | no | ✅ finishes | ❌ lost |
| __this PR__ | no | yes | ✅ finishes | ✅ kept |

The root cause is in rrweb, which leaves the rebuilt document open and only works without closing it. This reproduces with plain rrweb 2.2.0 (see the triage note), so it's worth reporting upstream separately.

prs.title: perf: don't refetch warm modules in reused runners
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- split from https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11752 (the warm-modules half)
- benchmark app https://github.com/vitest-dev/benchmarks/pull/2

Previously, a reused module runner (`isolate: false`) fetched a new warm-modules snapshot for every run request, which with several workers means every test file. Each snapshot walks the file's whole import graph on the main process and sends it over IPC. In a reused runner, though, most of that graph is already evaluated, and those imports never look at the snapshot. A snapshot only helps with modules that are new to this runner and that another worker has already transformed, and that help shrinks as the runner accumulates modules, while the walk still covers the whole graph.

This PR fetches the snapshot once per module runner and keeps it. In a multi-worker `isolate: false` run, that effectively turns warm modules off. Each runner's one snapshot is taken at its first file, when the server has transformed almost nothing yet.

### What changes

| setup | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `isolate: true`, vm pools | one snapshot per file, each for a new runner | same |
| `maxWorkers: 1` | one snapshot for the single request | same |
| `isolate: false`, several workers | one snapshot per file | one per runner, at its first file |

With `isolate: false` and several workers, main sends a snapshot of the file's import graph for many test files, but a worker has already evaluated most of it. Averages per test file, over all 800 test

prs.title: fix(browser): skip trace entries after their attempt ended
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11766

Previously, with trace view enabled, a browser action or `expect.element` that settled after its test attempt ended crashed inside Vitest.

```ts
test('unawaited', () => {
  page.getByRole('button').click().then(() => {})
})
```

```js
⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Unhandled Errors ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯
Vitest caught 1 unhandled error during the test run.
This might cause false positive tests. Resolve unhandled errors to make sure your tests are not affected.
⎯⎯⎯⎯ Unhandled Rejection ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startTime')
This error originated in "basic.test.ts" test file. It doesn't mean the error was thrown inside the file itself, but while it was running.
The last test to run before this error was "wait". This means either:
- the error was thrown while Vitest was running this test, or
- the error was thrown after the test completed, and this was the most recent test at that point.
⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯
```

This PR drops the trace entry when its attempt has already ended.

prs.title: fix(vm): reset fake timers after each test file (fix #11679)
prs.author: francesco-agnoletto
prs.body:
Fixes #11679

Follow up of #11380 as @shairez suggested there. Fake timers left on by a test file were never turned off, and in vm pools they also replace `hrtime` on the worker's `process`, which every file shares. That kept the context of every such file alive. This turns fake timers off after each file, next to the existing mocks reset.

I added a test that runs the existing leak probe fixture with a setup file that leaves fake timers on, it fails on main (5 of 5 contexts not released) and passes on this branch.

This only changes the vm pools runner. Can do the same in the other pools if you think it's needed.

prs.title: fix(cache): key module cache on the deps optimizer
prs.author: MO2k4
prs.body:
### Description

Written by an AI agent (Claude) on behalf of @MO2k4, who has reviewed it.

`fsModuleCache` keys a transform on its id, source and environment config, but the cached code imports optimized deps by path and version (`<cacheDir>/deps_ssr/<dep>.js?v=<browserHash>`). When the optimizer metadata changes while the source and config file don't (an `include` computed at load time, for example), or when another project with its own `cacheDir` filled the cache (#11773), the cached code imports a different copy of the dependency than the one `vi.mock` registers. Mocks are silently not applied, and the same dependency loads twice.

The key now also includes the environment's `cacheDir` and `browserHash` when it has a deps optimizer. `browserHash` is read on each call because the optimizer can re-run after `environmentHash` is memoized. Environments without an optimizer keep their keys.

Both new tests fail on main: one changes `deps.optimizer.ssr.include` between runs, the other is the two-project reproduction from #11773. The reproduction in #11774 fails on 5.0.5 and passes with `--no-fsModuleCache`.

Resolves #11773
Resolves #11774

prs.title: fix(ui): open trace view only for tests with a trace
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11766
- related https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11057

Previously, Vitest UI opened the trace view UI for any test selected in a file when `traceView` is enabled. However, with `traceView.mode: 'failure-only'` being the default, selecting any passing test with no artifacts ended up opening an empty pane with "No trace found". The editor also reserved an empty trace marker column for the same case.

This PR fixes it by triggering trace view UI features based on whether the test has trace artifacts instead of the global `traceView` config.

prs.title: refactor: remove stale worker-side invalidates handling
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- related to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11752
- findings https://gist.github.com/hi-ogawa/edb99430c4feac79e6af964bb8ce4441

Noticed a stale logic while trying to understand why `ctx.invalidates` check in https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11752 matters.

The worker invalidates the files in `ctx.invalidates` before running a test file. This is a leftover from when workers could survive the previous watch run and needed to drop stale modules. Since the v4 pool rewrite no worker outlives a run in watch reruns nor any programmatic test runs, so there is nothing stale to drop. The rest of the worker runtime already assumes this, for example, an already-evaluated module is answered from the worker's cache without asking the server (#9075).

This PR removes that worker-side handling. The one behavior change is in watch reruns with `isolate: false` and multiple workers where a reused worker received the same list with every test file, so it evaluated the changed modules again before each file.

For example, the e2e shows that rerun after editing a module that 6 test files import, `isolate: false`, `maxWorkers: 2` (same for `forks` and `threads`):

| | evaluations of the changed module |
|---|---:|
| before | 6 (one per test file) |
| after | 2 (one per worker) |

prs.title: feat: allow coverage providers to store data in fs module cache
prs.author: AriPerkkio
prs.body:
- Enables https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11686
- Related to https://github.com/vitest-dev/istanbuljs/pull/33

Allow coverage providers to return data that `fsModuleCache` will store **right next to** the cached module info. In https://github.com/vitest-dev/istanbuljs/pull/33 case, we want to avoid inlining instrumentation input source maps (_how transformed code at instrumentation phase remaps back to original sources, used during coverage remapping_) into the runtime code. This allows us to reduce code that's transferred to workers ~25%.

Coverage providers can define way to pass serializable data that `fsModuleCache` stores. When cache reads that file, it will call providers to instruct them about cache hit.
